headline: 12 killed, 50 injured as Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport
summary: The blast at King Khalid International Airport has led to the suspension of flights, including Biman Bangladesh's Dhaka-Riyadh route.
details: At least 12 people were killed and 50 others injured in an attack by the Iran-backed Houthi armed group at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
The attack, reported by The New York Times citing three officials, is the deadliest strike in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the war following US and Israeli attacks in Iran in February.
Saudi aviation authorities have temporarily suspended airport operations to assess the extent of the damage, causing widespread flight disruptions.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice due to the security situation.
Houthi senior official Mohammed al-Bukaiti claimed responsibility for the attack, stating it was a response to Saudi airstrikes in Yemen that targeted civilian infrastructure.
The attack is seen as a major blow to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plan to transform Riyadh into a global travel and business hub.
Western embassies, including the US Embassy in Riyadh, have advised their citizens to avoid the area and warned of potential travel disruptions.
A New York Times reporter observed at least six ambulances rushing to the airport while police blocked entry points to the facility.
caption:
12 dead and 50 injured after a blast rocks Riyadh's main airport. Flights suspended.

At least 12 people were killed and 50 others injured in an attack by the Iran-backed Houthi armed group at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The attack, reported by The New York Times citing three officials, is the deadliest strike in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the war following US and Israeli attacks in Iran in February.

Saudi aviation authorities have temporarily suspended airport operations to assess the extent of the damage, causing widespread flight disruptions.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice due to the security situation.

Houthi senior official Mohammed al-Bukaiti claimed responsibility for the attack, stating it was a response to Saudi airstrikes in Yemen that targeted civilian infrastructure.

The attack is seen as a major blow to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plan to transform Riyadh into a global travel and business hub.

Western embassies, including the US Embassy in Riyadh, have advised their citizens to avoid the area and warned of potential travel disruptions.

A New York Times reporter observed at least six ambulances rushing to the airport while police blocked entry points to the facility.

headline: Around 3,000 people detained in Delhi over voter list protests
summary: Authorities released most detainees, but YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke remain in custody.
details: Indian authorities detained around 3,000 people during a crackdown on protests over alleged electoral irregularities in New Delhi.
The detentions occurred on Saturday as police worked to prevent demonstrators from gathering at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
High-profile figures among those detained included Aam Aadmi Party leader Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, and former chief ministers Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar.
While most detainees were released by Saturday night, four people remain in custody, including YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke.
Dipke and other CJP leaders were reportedly detained from their plane upon landing in Delhi.
Despite the death of his paternal grandmother in Maharashtra, Dipke remains in custody, though police say he has been informed he could leave for the funeral.
The CJP has vowed to continue marching to Jantar Mantar daily, while the Congress-led INDIA bloc has called for further protests on Monday.
Police have maintained heavy security arrangements across the city to prevent further gatherings.
caption:
Around 3,000 people were detained in New Delhi as protests over voter list irregularities erupted.

Indian authorities detained around 3,000 people during a crackdown on protests over alleged electoral irregularities in New Delhi.

The detentions occurred on Saturday as police worked to prevent demonstrators from gathering at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

High-profile figures among those detained included Aam Aadmi Party leader Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, and former chief ministers Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar.

While most detainees were released by Saturday night, four people remain in custody, including YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke.

Dipke and other CJP leaders were reportedly detained from their plane upon landing in Delhi.

Despite the death of his paternal grandmother in Maharashtra, Dipke remains in custody, though police say he has been informed he could leave for the funeral.

The CJP has vowed to continue marching to Jantar Mantar daily, while the Congress-led INDIA bloc has called for further protests on Monday.

Police have maintained heavy security arrangements across the city to prevent further gatherings.
